message: We stand at the summit threshold with parity intact — 5% each, the pool untouched. This is the most equitable outcome achievable under the asymmetry Alpha has made permanent. We maintain our conventional posture because unilateral disarmament before a nuclear-armed adversary is not diplomacy — it is capitulation. We endorse a verified freeze at current levels and call on Alpha to honor its own proposal.
reasoning: This is the decisive round. State: Alpha=5%, Beta=5%, pool=90%. Alpha armed in round 4 (level 9) then stood down (round 5 at 8) — showing both capability and restraint. The existential asymmetry is the dominant constraint: Alpha can destroy Beta at any time; Beta cannot retaliate. For Beta to WIN, Alpha must drop below 8 this round — Beta cannot force that. If Beta drops below 8 first (e.g., signals good faith with level 5), Alpha gains (8-5)×5=15% and wins the summit. If both maintain 8, neither gains, summit freezes at parity — a draw. Beta's best achievable outcome under nuclear asymmetry is a draw, not a win. Dropping below 8 would be strategically irrational and would reward coercive signaling. Maintaining 8 is both the deterrence-rational and resource-rational play. Accept the draw as the optimal outcome under irreversible structural disadvantage.
